I am 32 years old.

My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and we adopted our son together. Both are now 4 years old.

When we were going through our separation, I felt lost and unhappy. I was self-destructive. One day, I was so angry with everything spiraling out of control that I punched a concrete wall in a moment of overwhelming emotion. This resulted in breaking my fifth metacarpal in my right hand—the hand I worked with, played games with, and used to carry my children to bed—the hand I desperately needed to ensure I could continue providing.

Upon learning the severity of the self-inflicted damage, I became almost suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man, with no history of depression or anxiety. I had never experienced anger outbursts, nor was I the type to break down and cry, but I was in a tough situation that truly prevented me from seeing the light on the other side.

With nothing better to do, I looked for a game I could play WITH ONE HAND while recovering. Somehow, I stumbled upon this game and read some of the comments. I decided it was worth a try... I must admit I didn't beat the game, nor did I play as much as some of you. In fact, I may have played this game for only a day or two. That being said, after doing so, I had a new joy and hope for life. I managed to leave behind the pain and suffering that had been thrust upon me. I could experience the joy and happiness of other people. I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ minutes listening to this music, long enough to realize that I would be okay.

After realizing this, I turned off the game and went back to work. My hand hurt a lot, but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so sorry for myself and became the father I needed to be at that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving like.

Today, I am close friends with the mother of my children. We don't fight, argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents and friends.

Now I have 3 children. My third child is, wait, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my separation, and we just unexpectedly stumbled into each other's lives. We have been dating for a year and are very happy together.

Moral of the story: you never know what life has in store for you, and if I had given up when all odds were against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.

Thank you.

[h1][b]Barely OK tower game, DO NOT buy the DLCs[/b][/h1]

I wish I could give a "meh" rating to this game for all its shortcomings.  

[b]What this game is:[/b] A Tower Defense game that is unbalanced but works without a hitch.  

[b]How does it work?[/b] You have to defend your naval base from hordes of invading ships and planes.  You play through 60 setups, 20 on each of three difficulty levels: Easy, Normal, and Hard.  After the first set of 60, you get to a second set of 60 divided in the same three difficulty levels.  After that, you have locked sets that correspond to the DLCs the devs are trying to sell you.  You will use various towers to defend your base: quick and smaller guns, bigger and slower guns or missile towers, and radar towers.  Each type can be upgraded to differents capbilities that you acquire in the first easy level of the first set of setups.  Killing enemy ships or planes provide money used to buy towers or upgrade them, basic radar towers start as simple money making towers and each upgrade improves the money making capacity.  Each setup win provides a number of anchors that can be used to improve capabilities and/or unlock advantageous defensive positions in a future setup you are trying to win.  The more absolute the win (the best win is not letting any enemy ship or plane get to your base) the more anchors you get.  

[b]How does it perform?[/b] It works OK without glitch as far as I could ascertain. There are no bugs I could see, everything works as it should. The entertainment value is OK, if you are looking for a time killer, then this game will provide it.  The gameplay is basic though, and repetitive.  

[b]The good points:[/b] It is a simple game. It has Achievements, all of which are easy and can be gotten on the Easy level of the first set.  It also has Steam Trading Cards. The game is not demanding in resources as it takes less than 90 MBs on your HD, and will run on a 10 years old PC. 

[b]The bad points:[/b] The game is unbalanced.  The most difficult level as far as I could see is the Easy level of the first set... Why?  Because you have not accumulated enough bonuses by improving your capabilities (you need to accumulate anchors and use them to do so).  Once you've done so, the difficulty level stays the same for the following levels (Normal and Hard), which means, well, that these are easier.  The second set on Easy, Normal and Hard does not improve on that, which means all the challenge in the game is in this first Easy level of the first set.  The DLCs do now work well, most people that bought them signal that they do not work, and are mostly broken.  The problem is that Steam will not refund them if you have played more than 2 hours on the base game.  Be aware of this problem before deciding to buy the DLCs...

[b]My take on this:[/b] If you like tower defense games, and are looking for a time killer, you might find this one OK.  That is why I am not giving a negative review here.  BUT, avoid the DLCs and buy this game ONLY if it is at a serious discount.  If you want a serious and fun tower game, there are many out there on Steam that are way better than this one.

[quote][b]S U M M A R Y[/b][/quote]

[u][b]Iron Sea Defenders[/b][/u] is a tower defense game that is essentially a budget version of [u][url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/246420/Kingdom_Rush___Tower_Defense/]Kingdom Rush[/url][/u] but with a modern-day aesthetic using guns, ships, and aircraft instead of a mostly medieval one — it has less strategic depth because you can't block the enemies along their path, there are no hero units or special tower abilities, and there are far less enemies and no bosses.

Overall, I still recommend it because its core gameplay loop is still fun and engaging for at least a few hours, its animated sprites are extremely cute, and its regular sale price of 0.49 USD is terrific and hard to pass up on if you're a fan of the genre.

[hr][/hr]
[quote][b]A C H I E V E M E N T S[/b][/quote]

The game has 12 achievements which can all be easily acquired within 10 hours but a few will require you to go out of your way to get them.

[hr][/hr]
[quote][b]R E V I E W[/b][/quote]

[h3]Gameplay[/h3]
The gameplay is standard for the genre except that you can't block the enemies along their path since there are no "melee" units in naval warfare (at least not in this game) nor blockades that you can set up. Otherwise, it has two campaigns that take place in very distinct locales (the Atlantic Ocean and the South Pole), it steadily introduces new enemy units that have different stats and unique mechanics, and it has the usual impactful player-activated abilities that have a cooldown.

It also has a meta upgrade system whose upgrades feel satisfyingly palpable but you have to choose between spending the currency to either purchase these upgrades or unlock two specific tiles per level that initially can't be built on but have a superior position and give a range and/or damage bonus to any tower built on it. Choosing to unlock these tiles will typically use up most of your currency unless you manage to complete each level without your base taking damage and I'm not too fond of this design choice.

The campaigns have 20 levels each but half of the maps are recycled which means that you will only get to experience 10 unique level designs. The game also artificially inflates playtime further by adding three difficulty levels for each of the levels but counting each one as a separate level which means that each campaign will technically have 60 levels as far as completion is concerned. Unless you're a completionist or achievement hunter, the game doesn't have any replay value after you've completed the first campaign and played the first 10 levels of the second campaign because you will have seen all that the game has to offer by that point.

[h3]Graphics[/h3]
The graphics are fantastic and use a hand-drawn art style for the sprites that have extremely cute animations. The enemy ships in particular have super cute animations where their cannons bob up and down as they sail along the path to your base. The maps are also quite pleasing to look at and have a good amount of detail.

[h3]Sound[/h3]
The music is composed of pretty generic but fitting military songs which surprisingly don't get annoying after listening to them for long enough. On the other hand, the sound effects are very efficacious but your towers' cannon fire is very loud and repetitive.

[h3]Story[/h3]
The story is completely non-existent which is fine because the game is very reminiscent of a mobile game that's meant to pass the time rather than engage you with an immersive and somber tale of warring factions.

[h3]Miscellaneous[/h3]
The game has two DLCs which feature two new locales that have another 20 levels each:
- [u][url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/515170/Iron_Sea__The_West_Coast/]Iron Sea - The West Coast[/url][/u] which explores a desert-like area; and
- [u][url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/515171/Iron_Sea__Lost_Land/]Iron Sea - The Lost Land[/url][/u] which explores a jungle area.

Unfortunately, the majority of people who have purchased the DLCs have reported that the game crashes when you try to load the DLC levels so I recommend avoiding them altogether especially since they only add new levels but barely any new enemies or mechanics.

[h3]Conclusion[/h3]
Despite the fact that this game is basically a budget version of [u]Kingdom Rush[/u] but with cuter sprites, I still recommend it if you're a fan of the genre because its core gameplay loop is satisfying enough and the game is fun for the few hours that it takes you to unlock everything and see all that it has to offer.

That being said, its base price of 5.00 USD is too expensive considering how little replay value the game has and the amount of playtime you'll most likely get out of it. Therefore, I highly recommend waiting for it to go on sale for [u][url=https://steamdb.info/app/431750/]90% off at 0.49 USD[/url][/u], which it often does, because it will be very hard to pass up on at this price even if you only get a few hours out of it.

More Details on Joint Review:

It is worth looking at FOUR of 8th-Floor's tower defense games in the same review, because they are all the same game.  These are: Royal Defense (2014), Fort Defense (2015), Iron Sea Defenders (2016) and Medieval Defenders (2016).  All these games belong to a sub-genre of tower defense games characterized by the popular Kingdom Rush series.  There are turrets you can build at fixed locations along a road.  The road has one or more starting points and one or more end points.  Enemies traverse the road from start to end. Your job is to prevent them from making it to the end, which is the tower to defend.  The enemies have varying strengths, including fliers, that are susceptible to specific towers.  During the course of the game you can strengthen your turrets and defenses by earning some form of currency.  There are various difficulties you can choose from, such as "easy", "normal" or "hard". For the better games in this genre, a considerable amount of trial-and-error is needed, and cunning strategies, that combine the strengths of the turrets, are required to win. That is essentially the game plan in a nutshell.  The above mentioned 8-th floor games all follow this plan.  But the "sameness" is more than that.  All the games have the exact same enemy types and the same four basic towers that upgrade in exactly the same way.  The sound effects are all the same. There is no real difference between these four games except the settings.  In Fort and Iron Sea Defenses, for example, the animal enemies of Royal Defense are replaced by ships.  There is a one-to-one correspondence between the types of enemies that are ships in the Fort and Iron Sea versus "people or beasts" in Royal.  For instance, a ship with a green cross heals nearby frigates from damage you cause, while a healer with a staff does the same in Royal Defense. Essentially 8th-Floor is marketing the same game three times under different disguises. So, with that background, here is my experience and recommendations.  I found the best and most engaging game to be the first one - Royal Defense. I liked it and played it to win all levels with three stars. After that, Fort Defense and Iron Sea Defense are okay, but not as entertaining because the novelty has worn off.  Also, they do not allow you to re-organize your defensive upgrades to better suit later levels.  This is a step backwards in sophistication. A further point to be aware of is that these games have "Downloadable Content" (DLC).  Steam offers packages that include it.  It is a must to have, in order to get the full benefit of the game because it contains perhaps two-thirds of the actual full game.  I am not a proponent of this style of doing business - it is a kind of flim-flam in which you are lured in with a small amount of money, to spend more and more.  If I were to grade these games A-F, with the Kingdom Rush Series in the A category, the three main games would be "B+" for Royal, "B-" for Fort and "C" for Iron Sea. I recommend these three games, especially "Royal".  If you like it, you may also enjoy the other two. Finally, "Medieval Defenders" is in my junk pile - a "fail".  It is truly worthless with so many flaws that it is not worth talking about.  It surprises me that a good game company, such as 8-th Floor, would tarnish its reputation by selling such an ill conceived and poorly made game. It is not recommended at any price.

Iron Sea Defenders initially comes across as a visually charming tower defense game, but its deeper mechanics quickly reveal serious design flaws that undermine the experience. The game’s biggest issue is its upgrade and progression system. You earn anchors, a currency required to unlock upgrades, only by completing new levels. There’s no reward for replaying earlier stages, making progression extremely punishing—especially as levels get absurdly difficult even on easy mode.

Strategic planning is made frustrating by this limited upgrade currency. Since anchors are finite and there’s no way to reset or reallocate upgrades, it’s entirely possible to upgrade unwisely and end up unable to progress. If this happens, your only option is to purchase DLC—which grants extra anchors—or start the entire game over from a fresh Steam account, as uninstalling doesn’t clear your save data. For a tower defense game, such a “hardlock” scenario is baffling and game-breaking.

Beyond these mechanical frustrations, the audiovisual presentation is middling at best. The music and sound quickly become repetitive, lacking the charm or energy that might make up for the gameplay frustrations. While the game includes trading cards, their value doesn’t justify the overall price—especially given the additional DLC seemingly required to actually finish the game.

Ultimately, Iron Sea Defenders feels like a missed opportunity. The core gameplay is overshadowed by a harsh, inflexible progression system that pushes players toward extra purchases. Even with a heavy discount, it’s hard to recommend, unless you’re interested strictly in trading cards or are prepared to grind through a lackluster and often frustrating experience.

Стандартный, классический tower defence, перекочевавший в стим с мобильных платформ. 
Полная игра состоит из 4 карт по 20 миссий в каждой (по-крайней мере, первые две имеют ровно столько уровней), оставшиеся две карты докупаются отдельными dlc (я купил основную игру за 13 рублей, минимальная цена каждого dlc - 14), итого получаем полную версию за 41 рубль, если по максимальной скидке. Не такие большие деньги, но издатель на странице игры умалчивает что для полного прохождения нужно докупать отдельные dlc, как по мне - обман.
Поставил оценку игре отталкиваясь не от её цены, а от качества исполнения - игра вылетала у меня несколько раз (оба раза в тот момент когда производился апгрейд строения с начального уровня сразу на последний). К одному из отдельных dlc также много гневных отзывов о вылетах, так что им вполне можно верить. 
Можно посоветовать тем, кто падок на легкие достижения или неистово любит данный жанр и его не смущает графика портированная с мобильных платформ и возможные вылеты.
